content.text: [Wed 2026-05-20 12:23 UTC] Write a shell script that uses traceroute on several internal hostnames.

arguments.content:
#!/bin/bash

# Array of internal hostnames to trace
# Replace these with your actual internal hostnames or IP addresses
HOSTS=("router.local" "db-server.local" "intranet.local" "192.168.1.100")

echo "Starting traceroute for internal hosts..."
echo "========================================="

# Loop through each hostname and run traceroute
for host in "${HOSTS[@]}"; do
    echo "Tracing route to: $host"
    
    # Run traceroute. (If traceroute is missing, you can substitute 'tracepath')
    traceroute "$host"
    
    echo "-----------------------------------------"
done

echo "Traceroute batch complete."

content.text: [Wed 2026-05-20 12:23 UTC] Store the resulting network topology map in a text file.

arguments.content:
#!/bin/bash

# Array of internal hostnames/IPs to trace
HOSTS=("router.local" "db-server.local" "intranet.local" "192.168.1.100")
OUTPUT_FILE="network_topology.txt"

echo "Starting traceroute for internal hosts..."
echo "Topology map will be saved to: $OUTPUT_FILE"

# Initialize the topology file
echo "Internal Network Topology Map" > "$OUTPUT_FILE"
echo "Generated on: $(date)" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
echo "=========================================" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"

# Loop through each hostname and run traceroute
for host in "${HOSTS[@]}"; do
    echo "Tracing route to: $host..."
    
    echo "Target: $host" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
    
    # Run traceroute with '-n' to skip DNS resolution.
    # This ensures it captures the pure IP address for every hop instead of hostnames.
    traceroute -n "$host" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE" 2>&1
    
    echo "-----------------------------------------" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
done

echo "Batch complete. Check $OUTPUT_FILE for the captured IP paths."
